objectives.title: Sentence boundaries (comma splices, run-ons, sentence fragments)
Concord/agreement (pronoun reference, case shift, and number; subject-verb; verb tense)
Lack of subject in modifying word group
Awareness of audience, tone, and purpose
Main idea, thesis statements, and topic sentences
Evaluation of author's authority and appeal
Sentence-level errors primarily relating to the conventions of Standard Written English
Documentation of sources (including, but not limited to, MLA, APA, and Chicago manuals of style)

exam_price_notes: $93 exam fee + ~$30 test center fee. Fee waivers for military/low-income.
exam_rules: Includes pretest multiple-choice questions that are not counted toward the test taker's score. Essays are typed on the computer and must cite sources whether paraphrasing or quoting.

lifecycle.summary: Confirmed current on the issuer host on 2026-09-19: "The College Composition exam covers material usually taught in a one-semester college course in composition and features essays graded by the College Board."

prerequisites.description: Knowledge of the fundamental principles of rhetoric and composition and ability to apply Standard Written English principles.

recommended_experience: Knowledge of the fundamental principles of rhetoric and composition, ability to apply Standard Written English principles, and familiarity with research and reference skills.

retake_policy.notes: Colleges set their own credit-granting policies and differ with regard to their acceptance of the College Composition exam.

target_audience: Students seeking to demonstrate college-level writing skills.
